newsitem.title: USA: NHL-CAMPBELL AGREES TO CONTRACT EXTENSION WITH RANGERS.
newsitem.headline: NHL-CAMPBELL AGREES TO CONTRACT EXTENSION WITH RANGERS.

text.p: New York Rangers head coach Colin Campbell, who guided the team through a stirring run to the NHL Eastern Conference finals, agreed to a contract extension, the club announced Tuesday.
Terms were not disclosed, but Campbell reportedly received a two-year extension worth about $1.4 million through the 1999-2000 season. He was entering the final year of his current contract.

"Colin has done an outstanding job for us, and of all the people in the organisation that helped us get to where we we got in the playoffs, he probably did the most of anybody," Rangers general manager Neil Smith said.
"His experience and leadership has been an invaluable asset to the club," added Smith.

The Rangers finished in fifth-place in the East with a mediocre 38-34-10 record. But despite a rash of injuries, the team raised its game in playoffs to upset the Florida Panthers and New Jersey Devils before falling to the Philadelphia Flyers in the Stanley Cup semifinals.
The 44-year-old Campbell has a 101-84-27 record in three years as Rangers coach. He succeeded Mike Keenan, who left immediately after the team's Stanley Cup championship in 1994.
Campbell was interviewed last month by Team Canada general manager Bob Clarke for Canada's head coaching position at the Nagano Olympics in February.
